en.greeting: Hi! Today you build bigger words: 'not' prefixes like im- and ir-, new endings like -ness and -ity, and compound words like deadline.

steps.title: in- changes with the sound
steps.text: Quick recap first: un- and dis- mean not, re- means again. Now meet their cousin, in-.
steps.body:
**in-** also means *not*: *incorrect, inexpensive* (cheap!). Its spelling follows the **first letter** of the word:
- before **p / m** → **im-**: *impatient, immature*
- before **r** → **ir-**: *irregular, irrelevant*
- before **l** → **il-**: *illogical, illiterate*
With m, r and l you get a **double letter**: *im + mature*. Indonesian writes *ilegal, irasional* with one letter; English doubles it: **illegal, irrational**.

steps.title: A pattern, not a law
steps.text: Read these out loud and look at the prefix in each one.
steps.body: The pattern tells you **how in- changes**, not **whether** a word takes in-. Some p, r and l words take un- or dis-: *unpopular, unreliable, unlikely, disloyal*. So learn each word with its prefix, and check a dictionary. But if a word does take in-, the sound decides: 'unpossible' is wrong, it's **impossible**.

examples.en: Passengers get impatient when the KRL is late.
examples.id: Penumpang jadi tidak sabar kalau KRL terlambat.

examples.en: Some of the figures in the report are incorrect.
examples.id: Beberapa angka di laporan itu salah.

examples.en: My shifts at the hospital are irregular.
examples.id: Jadwal shift saya di rumah sakit tidak teratur.

examples.en: The new parking rule is very unpopular.
examples.id: Aturan parkir yang baru sangat tidak disukai.

examples.en: The Wi-Fi on this floor is unreliable.
examples.id: Wi-Fi di lantai ini tidak bisa diandalkan.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Choose the right word.

question.prompt: Dimas left the office door unlocked all weekend. That was really ___ of him.
question.explanation: **responsible** starts with r, so in- becomes **ir-** and the r is doubled: *irresponsible*. 'unresponsible' is a very common mistake (wrong prefix), and 'iresponsible' is missing one r.

steps.title: Nouns: -ness, -ity, -ment
steps.text: Now the end of the word: endings that make nouns.
steps.body:
A **noun** names a thing or an idea. Three endings make one:
- **-ness** after an adjective: *kind → kindness, aware → awareness, weak → weakness*
- **-ity** after an adjective: *able → ability, responsible → responsibility, possible → possibility*
- **-ment** after a verb (from B1): *manage → management*
No rule for -ness or -ity: learn each one. Spelling: *happy → happiness*, *-ble → -bility*. Like Indonesian *sadar → kesadaran*.

steps.title: Adjectives and adverbs
steps.text: More endings: these make describing words.
steps.body: Adjectives: **-ive** (*creative, attractive*), **-al** (*national, professional*), **-ous** (*dangerous, famous*), **-ful** (*successful*). Add **-ly** for an adverb, a word that says **how**: *professionally, easily*. Slot rule from B1: after **be / very** or before a noun → adjective; after a verb → adverb. So not 'very success' but **very successful**. Careful: *friendly* ends in -ly but is an adjective.

examples.en: Our new office is in a very attractive building.
examples.id: Kantor baru kami ada di gedung yang sangat menarik.

examples.en: Crossing this road at night is dangerous.
examples.id: Menyeberang jalan ini malam hari itu berbahaya.

examples.en: Bandung is famous for its factory outlets.
examples.id: Bandung terkenal dengan factory outlet-nya.

examples.en: She handled the angry customer very professionally.
examples.id: Dia menangani pelanggan yang marah itu dengan sangat profesional.

examples.en: With the new app, you can book a train ticket easily.
examples.id: Dengan aplikasi baru, kamu bisa pesan tiket kereta dengan mudah.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Which form fits the gap?

question.prompt: Bu Ani explains new ideas clearly and ___, so her team always understands what to do.
question.explanation: The gap says **how** she explains, and it's joined to the adverb *clearly* with *and*: you need another adverb, **effectively** (effective + -ly). *effective* is the adjective and *effectiveness* is a noun.

steps.title: Compound words
steps.text: Last part: two words that work as one.
steps.body:
A **compound** is two words used as one. Three spellings:
- **one word**: *deadline, workplace, feedback*
- **hyphen**: *user-friendly, well-known, long-term, time-consuming*
- **two words**: *credit card, bus stop*
There's no rule for the spelling: check a dictionary. The **main word comes last**: a *bus stop* is a stop. Indonesian is the opposite (*halte bus, kartu kredit*), so not 'card credit'.

steps.title: Compounds in sentences
steps.text: Notice the spelling of each compound.
steps.body: Compound adjectives usually have a **hyphen**, especially before a noun: *a long-term plan*. With a number, the noun stays singular: *a two-hour meeting*, not 'two-hours'.

examples.en: We need your feedback before the deadline on Friday.
examples.id: Kami perlu masukanmu sebelum tenggatnya hari Jumat.

examples.en: Checking every receipt by hand is time-consuming.
examples.id: Memeriksa setiap struk dengan tangan itu makan waktu.

examples.en: Saving a little every month is a good long-term plan.
examples.id: Menabung sedikit setiap bulan adalah rencana jangka panjang yang bagus.

examples.en: Our manager wants a two-hour meeting this afternoon.
examples.id: Manajer kami mau rapat dua jam sore ini.

examples.en: The bus stop is in front of the bank.
examples.id: Halte busnya ada di depan bank.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pick the compound that fits.

question.prompt: Even my grandmother can pay her bills with this app. It's really ___.
question.explanation: If even a grandmother can use it, the app is easy to use: **user-friendly** (mudah dipakai). *time-consuming* means it takes a lot of time, and *long-term* is about the future (jangka panjang).

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Main word last!

question.solution: The meeting room is on the third floor.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Ruang rapatnya ada di lantai tiga.
question.explanation: *ruang rapat* is a room, so **room** comes last: *meeting room*. Indonesian puts the main word first, English puts it last ('room meeting' ✗).

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu membentuk kata yang lebih besar: prefix 'tidak' seperti im- dan ir-, akhiran baru seperti -ness dan -ity, dan kata majemuk seperti deadline.

steps.title: in- berubah mengikuti bunyi
steps.text: Ulang sebentar dulu: un- dan dis- artinya tidak, re- artinya lagi. Sekarang kenalan dengan saudaranya, in-.
steps.body:
**in-** juga berarti *tidak*: *incorrect, inexpensive* (murah!). Ejaannya mengikuti **huruf pertama** kata dasarnya:
- sebelum **p / m** → **im-**: *impatient, immature*
- sebelum **r** → **ir-**: *irregular, irrelevant*
- sebelum **l** → **il-**: *illogical, illiterate*
Dengan m, r dan l hurufnya jadi **dobel**: *im + mature*. Bahasa Indonesia menulis *ilegal, irasional* dengan satu huruf; bahasa Inggris dobel: **illegal, irrational**.

steps.title: Pola, bukan hukum
steps.text: Baca dengan suara keras dan perhatikan prefix di setiap kalimat.
steps.body: Polanya memberi tahu **bagaimana in- berubah**, bukan **apakah** kata itu memakai in-. Beberapa kata p, r dan l memakai un- atau dis-: *unpopular, unreliable, unlikely, disloyal*. Jadi hafalkan setiap kata bersama prefix-nya, dan cek kamus. Tapi kalau kata itu memang memakai in-, bunyinya yang menentukan: 'unpossible' salah, yang benar **impossible**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pilih kata yang benar.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas left the office door unlocked all weekend. That was really ___ of him.
question.explanation: **responsible** diawali r, jadi in- menjadi **ir-** dan r-nya dobel: *irresponsible* (tidak bertanggung jawab). 'unresponsible' kesalahan yang sangat sering (prefix-nya salah), dan 'iresponsible' kurang satu r.

steps.title: Kata benda: -ness, -ity, -ment
steps.text: Sekarang bagian belakang kata: akhiran yang membuat kata benda.
steps.body:
**Kata benda** adalah kata untuk benda atau hal. Tiga akhiran ini membuatnya:
- **-ness** setelah kata sifat: *kind → kindness, aware → awareness, weak → weakness*
- **-ity** setelah kata sifat: *able → ability, responsible → responsibility, possible → possibility*
- **-ment** setelah kata kerja (dari B1): *manage → management*
Tidak ada aturan untuk -ness atau -ity: hafalkan per kata. Ejaan: *happy → happiness*, *-ble → -bility*. Mirip *sadar → kesadaran*.

steps.title: Kata sifat dan adverb
steps.text: Akhiran lain: yang ini membuat kata yang menjelaskan.
steps.body: Kata sifat: **-ive** (*creative, attractive*), **-al** (*national, professional*), **-ous** (*dangerous, famous*), **-ful** (*successful*). Tambah **-ly** untuk adverb, kata yang menjelaskan **bagaimana**: *professionally, easily*. Aturan posisi dari B1: setelah **be / very** atau sebelum kata benda → kata sifat; setelah kata kerja → adverb. Jadi bukan 'very success' tapi **very successful**. Hati-hati: *friendly* berakhiran -ly tapi kata sifat.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Bentuk mana yang cocok?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Bu Ani explains new ideas clearly and ___, so her team always understands what to do.
question.explanation: Titik-titiknya menjelaskan **bagaimana** dia menjelaskan, dan disambung dengan adverb *clearly* memakai *and*: kamu butuh adverb lagi, **effectively** (effective + -ly). *effective* adalah kata sifat dan *effectiveness* kata benda.

steps.title: Kata majemuk
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: dua kata yang bekerja sebagai satu.
steps.body:
**Kata majemuk** adalah dua kata yang dipakai sebagai satu. Tiga cara menulisnya:
- **satu kata**: *deadline, workplace, feedback*
- **tanda hubung**: *user-friendly, well-known, long-term, time-consuming*
- **dua kata**: *credit card, bus stop*
Tidak ada aturan untuk ejaannya: cek kamus. **Kata utamanya di belakang**: *bus stop* adalah halte (stop). Bahasa Indonesia kebalikannya (*halte bus, kartu kredit*), jadi bukan 'card credit'.

steps.title: Kata majemuk dalam kalimat
steps.text: Perhatikan ejaan setiap kata majemuk.
steps.body: Kata sifat majemuk biasanya pakai **tanda hubung**, terutama sebelum kata benda: *a long-term plan*. Dengan angka, kata bendanya tetap tunggal: *a two-hour meeting*, bukan 'two-hours'.

examples.id: Kami perlu masukanmu sebelum tenggatnya hari Jumat.

examples.en: Checking every receipt by hand is time-consuming.
examples.id: Memeriksa setiap struk dengan tangan itu makan waktu.

examples.en: Saving a little every month is a good long-term plan.
examples.id: Menabung sedikit setiap bulan adalah rencana jangka panjang yang bagus.

examples.en: Our manager wants a two-hour meeting this afternoon.
examples.id: Manajer kami mau rapat dua jam sore ini.

examples.en: The bus stop is in front of the bank.
examples.id: Halte busnya ada di depan bank.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pilih kata majemuk yang cocok.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Even my grandmother can pay her bills with this app. It's really ___.
question.explanation: Kalau nenek pun bisa memakainya, aplikasinya mudah dipakai: **user-friendly**. *time-consuming* artinya makan waktu, dan *long-term* tentang masa depan (jangka panjang).

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Kata utama di belakang!

question.solution: The meeting room is on the third floor.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Ruang rapatnya ada di lantai tiga.
question.explanation: *ruang rapat* adalah ruangan, jadi **room** di belakang: *meeting room*. Bahasa Indonesia menaruh kata utama di depan, bahasa Inggris di belakang ('room meeting' ✗).
